verdict_text:
YES

The script drops exactly the 48 buffers via `fullmatch`, casts exactly the 64 listed projection matrices to bfloat16 (`.float().to(torch.bfloat16)`, equivalent to the specified direct cast), upcasts every remaining tensor to float32, preserves names, asserts all four required checks before writing, and writes to `out/T3` with a 268,435,456-byte shard limit. The sharding/index behavior itself lives in the unshown `_ckpt.save_sharded_safetensors`, so that clause is not verifiable from this file alone.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
